messages:
jordan: FYI we have a canary GPU pool rollout to staging scheduled tomorrow 09:00 UTC. Before we bring nodes up we need extra IPv4 capacity — specifically EIPs + ENIs per AZ. Current account quotas will block scale.
lee: how many EIPs/ENIs are we asking for? also which AWS account/region? :thinking_face:
jordan: Region: eu-west-1 (staging). Expected peak: 25 GPU nodes across 3 AZs. Design uses one EIP per node for our node-level NAT in the new subnet. Requesting 120 EIPs total (includes 20% headroom), and bump ENI quota to 200 (we currently have 60). Also need VPC elastic IP association limits increased and permission to allocate more private IPv4s per ENI.
anika: Can we avoid so many EIPs by using central NAT gateways? NAT gateway cost is high for egress we measured. For canary we prefer per-node EIP so outgoing IPs are stable for downstream allowlists.
maria: cost note: 120 extra EIPs + more ENIs is cheap in allotment terms, but if we keep them allocated long-term the monthly EIP charges apply. For canary it's fine if we release after 2 weeks.
lee: ok. I'll open an AWS support case. Suggest we file two quota increase requests: "Elastic IPs (All)" -> +120, and "Network interfaces per VPC"/per account -> +150. Also add "IP addresses per ENI" if provider enforces.
jordan: thanks. Can you paste a copyable case body?
lee: sure — putting template below. Use the account id: 123456789012 and tag it with priority: low but with "needed-by" 2026-03-18 09:00 UTC.
```
Subject: Quota increase request for Elastic IPs and ENIs — staging canary GPU pool
Account ID: 123456789012
Region: eu-west-1
Requested increases:
 - Elastic IPs (All): increase by 120 (total requested 140)
 - Network interfaces per account/VPC: increase by 150 (total requested 210)
Reason: Spinning up a canary GPU node pool for staging that allocates one EIP per node to provide stable egress IPs for downstream allowlists. Expected nodes: 25 across 3 AZs; request includes 20% buffer for rollout and burst. Needed by: 2026-03-18 09:00 UTC
Additional notes: We will release unused EIPs after 2 weeks. Please advise if there are alternative quotas to request (e.g., ENI per subnet) to ensure successful node provisioning.
```
lee: pinging @aws-support-bot to create case now.
aws-support-bot: AWS support case created: case-id-9876543210. Estimated response 48-72 hours.
anika: 48-72h is cutting it close. Can we do a short-term workaround: create a cross-account NAT account with shared NAT gateways and allocate fewer EIPs? Then update security allowlists to point at NAT IPs. That would reduce EIP count to ~6-9.
jordan: good thought. For canary we need stable per-node IPs for tracing upstream per-node telemetry tags — central NAT would erase that granularity. So prefer EIPs for now.
maria: ops question — do we need ENI quota in every AZ? AWS quota is often per region. Confirm with support case to ensure AZ-specific limits won't block.
lee: added that to the case body. Also attaching a small `eksctl` snippet showing nodegroup spec that triggers EIP allocs:
```
nodeGroups:
  - name: gpu-canary
    instanceType: p4d.24xlarge
    desiredCapacity: 8
    maxSize: 25
    tags:
      role: gpu-canary
networking:
  clusterEndpoints: public
```
lee: assigning to @anika to follow-up with support and escalate if needed.
anika: will monitor case and try to get an interim manual approval. If we get a slow response, plan B is to spin 6 NAT gateways and use per-node ephemeral EIPs for test runners only.
jordan: thanks. Please update this thread when case moves or if we need to postpone rollout. :+1:
deploy-bot: Reminder scheduled: canary rollout job gpu-canary -> staging at 2026-03-18T09:00:00Z.
lee: case-id-9876543210 updated: AWS asked for justification docs and network diagram. Uploading in 10m.
anika: uploaded diagram and justification. Support increased Elastic IPs to 140 (temporary) — they set TTL 30 days. ENI increase pending.
jordan: great, that should unblock initial canary. Closing action: track ENI increase and confirm when nodes can reach desired 25.
maria: I'll coordinate cost tracking and ensure release plan after canary.
lee: will follow up when ENI quota is approved.
